# Recourse Contact Templates

Use these when a session results in damage or an overstay situation.
Always contact the customer BEFORE initiating any Stripe charge.
Document that you sent this message (screenshot or email timestamp) — it's your chargeback defense.

---

## Template 1 — Damage Notice (Initial Contact)

**Subject:** Your Tee365 session on [DATE] — equipment damage

Hi [FIRST NAME],

Thanks for visiting Tee365 on [DATE]. We hope you enjoyed your session.

During our post-session inspection we found damage to [DESCRIBE: e.g., "Bay 2's impact screen" / "one of the provided clubs (7-iron)"] that occurred during your time slot. We reviewed our footage and wanted to reach out directly before taking any further steps.

The estimated cost to repair/replace is **$[AMOUNT]**.

We'd love to resolve this directly with you. If you have any questions or believe there's been a mistake, please reply to this message within **48 hours** and we'll sort it out together.

If we don't hear back, we'll proceed with a charge of $[AMOUNT] to the card on file associated with your booking, per the terms you agreed to at booking.

Thanks for understanding — we're a small operation and keeping the equipment in great shape is what keeps the bays affordable for everyone.

Jerrod
Tee365 Indoor Golf
[PHONE / EMAIL]

---

## Template 2 — Overstay Notice (Initial Contact)

**Subject:** Your Tee365 session on [DATE] — overstay

Hi [FIRST NAME],

Thanks for coming in on [DATE]. Glad you had a good time.

Our records show your session was booked from [START TIME] to [END TIME]. Our policy allows a 15-minute grace period, after which additional time is billed at your booked hourly rate of $[RATE]/hr. Your session extended to approximately [ACTUAL END TIME], resulting in [X] additional minutes beyond the grace period.

The overstay charge is **$[AMOUNT]**.

If you think there's an error, reply within **48 hours** and we'll take a look. Otherwise we'll apply a charge of $[AMOUNT] to your card on file per the terms agreed to at booking.

No hard feelings — just keeping things fair for the next customer whose session starts right after yours.

Jerrod
Tee365 Indoor Golf
[PHONE / EMAIL]

---

## Template 3 — Follow-Up (No Response After 48 Hours)

**Subject:** Follow-up: Tee365 session on [DATE]

Hi [FIRST NAME],

Following up on my message from [DATE OF FIRST CONTACT] regarding [damage to X / overstay of X minutes] from your session on [SESSION DATE].

We haven't heard back, so we'll be processing a charge of **$[AMOUNT]** to your card on file today. You'll receive a receipt from Stripe.

If you'd like to discuss this, you're welcome to reply or call us at [PHONE]. We're always open to working something out directly.

Jerrod
Tee365 Indoor Golf

---

## Template 4 — Charge Notification (Sent Same Day as Charge)

**Subject:** Tee365 charge of $[AMOUNT] — [DATE]

Hi [FIRST NAME],

A charge of **$[AMOUNT]** has been applied to your card on file (ending in [LAST 4]) for [damage to X / overstay on DATE]. You'll see this appear as "Tee365" on your statement.

A receipt has been sent separately by Stripe.

If you have questions, reply here or call [PHONE].

Jerrod
Tee365 Indoor Golf

## Process Checklist

When an incident occurs, work through this in order:

- [ ] Note the issue with timestamp (damage found / session end time observed)
- [ ] Pull and save relevant camera footage
- [ ] Take photos of any physical damage
- [ ] Look up customer name, email, and booking details in admin panel
- [ ] Send Template 1 or 2
- [ ] Wait 48 hours
- [ ] If no response → send Template 3, initiate Stripe charge same day
- [ ] Send Template 4 on the day of charge
- [ ] Log the incident: date, customer, issue, amount, resolution
